title: Ensure 'Access this computer from the network' is set to 'Administrators, Authenticated Users, ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS' (DC only)
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 2.2.2: Ensure 'Access this computer from the network' is set to 'Administrators, Authenticated Users, ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS' (DC only)

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

fields.name: audit_output
fields.description: Raw output from the audit command

steps.name: Check if the system is a Domain Controller or `(Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).ProductType`
steps.function: 1. Check if the system is a Domain Controller using command: `wmic os get ProductType /value` or `(Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).ProductType`. Expected result: ProductType=2 (Domain Controller). If not a Domain Controller, SKIP this checkpoint.

steps.name: Check the 'Access this computer from the network' user right assignment
steps.function: 2. Check the 'Access this computer from the network' user right assignment using command: `secedit /export /cfg $env:TEMP\secpol.cfg; Get-Content $env:TEMP\secpol.cfg | Select-String 'SeNetworkLogonRight'`. Expected result: SeNetworkLogonRight = *S-1-5-32-544,*S-1-5-11,*S-1-5-9 (Administrators, Authenticated Users, ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS).

steps.name: Check the 'Access this computer from the network' setting via registry
steps.function: 3. Check the 'Access this computer from the network' setting via registry using command: `Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name 'SeNetworkLogonRight' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`. Expected result: Value contains SIDs for Administrators (S-1-5-32-544), Authenticated Users (S-1-5-11), and ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS (S-1-5-9).

steps.name: Check the effective user right assignment or `Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_UserAccount` combined with `secedit…
steps.function: 4. Check the effective user right assignment using command: `whoami /priv` or `Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_UserAccount` combined with `secedit /export`. Expected result: The exported security policy shows SeNetworkLogonRight assigned exactly to Administrators, Authenticated Users, and ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS with no additional or missing principals.

steps.name: Summarize overall compliance status: PASS if the system is a Domain Controller and SeNetworkLogonRight is set exactly…
steps.function: 5. Summarize overall compliance status: PASS if the system is a Domain Controller and SeNetworkLogonRight is set exactly to Administrators, Authenticated Users, and ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS; SKIP if the system is not a Domain Controller; FAIL if the system is a Domain Controller but the user right assignment is missing, has extra principals, or is misconfigured.

computations._cis_status: PASS if audit output contains '** PASS **', FAIL if '** FAIL **', SKIP otherwise

steps.name: Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance…
steps.function: 6. Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR) derived from the last requirement's status variable.

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
The audit script must be read-only: it may create a temporary export file for secedit but must remove it afterward and must not modify any system settings.
reference_procedure: Navigate to the UI Path articulated in the Remediation section and confirm it is set as prescribed.
